about: Additions to bridge-contract.json that work both ways, so they do not feed its hash and keep the bridge id (ios/architecture.md D3, D14). Two kinds only. An optional trailing argument: an app built before it sends one fewer, and the engine must answer as it did before when the argument is undefined. An optional return field: an engine built before it leaves it out, and the app must read its absence as none; an app built before it ignores a field it does not know. Anything else, or anything an older app cannot do without, belongs in bridge-contract.json and is a new bridge. bridge.test.ts and EngineBridgeContractTests.swift count each door's arity as its contract args plus these; bridge.test.ts also checks each optional argument trails the contract ones by name and that a call with only the contract args answers as one with them undefined. An optional return field's absence is tested per feature (US-61: USProductsTests). A real bridge change never goes here.

historyJson.optionalReturns: rows[].bound and rows[].note (US-12 AC20): a lab result printed as a limit carries bound, its number in the row's unit, and its value reads "> 60"; the chart plots it at bound, hollow and out of the line. note is the plan's word on a current limit it cannot grade, shown in place of "Used in your plan". An engine before them sends neither, so the app draws every point from value as before; an app before them finds no number in a limit's value, so it leaves that point off the chart and still lists it with its symbol.

screenJson.optionalReturns: plan.usProducts: us-products.ts's usProductSections, the [PlanSection] ready to draw, for isUS true (the App Store storefront USA) and a known adult: on the Supplements section each product card's suggestion carries usProduct {product, name, line, url} and its US description and references, and the section carries ownershipLine. Left out when no block shows (US-61). An app before it sends no isUS, so it gets none; an engine before it sends no usProducts, so the app draws the plain sections. Its first shape (2026-10-31, {blocks, ownershipLine}) was read by no shipped app, so the change is safe for builds 3 and 4. Also myData.vitals[], bloodTests[] and psa rows' target (health-core rowTarget(...).bare, or null) and previous (the newest earlier day's value in the row's units, or null), US-62 AC8/AC9: an engine before them sends neither, and the app draws the row with its date alone and no bracketed value; an app before them ignores both.
